result.question: I'd rather take Transformer 1 at site MAIN out of service once than three times. Pull every open and pending-approval work order on it. For each one, give me the number, description, priority and scheduled date, and say whether it needs the unit de-energized, for example internal inspection, OLTC work or electrical testing, or whether it can be done live, for example oil sampling. Group the outage-needing work orders into bundles. Each bundle must have at least two work orders whose scheduled dates fall within 14 days of each other. For each bundle, propose a single outage date where the MAIN calendar has the fewest other scheduled work orders. Estimate each bundle's total planned hours, using the planned hours on the work orders themselves. Where a work order has no plan, use the average actual hours of closed work orders on Transformer 1. Then check the latest acetylene and hydrogen. If acetylene is above 1 ppm, any bundle with OLTC or inspection work moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load. If fewer than two outage-needing work orders exist, don't bundle anything. Recommend whether each one should be done alone or deferred to the next planned outage, and why.
result.answer:
## Transformer 1 (MAIN) — Open / Pending-Approval Work Orders

Only **one** work order exists on Transformer 1 in any status (I scanned all 3 MAIN work orders to rule out variant asset names; the other two are on PUMP3 and CHILLER6).

| WO # | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled date | Outage required? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1000051** | OLTC inspection – on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); confirmatory oil sample for lab DGA at the visit | 1 (highest) | WAPPR (pending approval) | **None** – no schedstart / targstart set | **Yes – de-energized.** OLTC internal inspection requires the unit out of service. (The attached oil sample could be done live, but it's folded into the same visit.) |

**Planned hours:** None – the WO has no `estlabhrs` and no labor plan (`wplabor` is null). Fallback also not available: there are **no closed work orders on Transformer 1**, so an average actual hours figure cannot be computed. Hours are unestimated; a typical OLTC internal inspection with oil sampling is a full-day job, but that's a rule-of-thumb, not a data-derived figure.

## Bundling

**No bundles formed.** Only one outage-needing work order exists, which is below the two-WO minimum, so per your rule nothing is bundled and no calendar-optimized outage date is proposed.

## Latest DGA check

Newest reading (timestamp **2024-01-19** — note this is ~2.7 years stale; there is no newer telemetry on this asset):

- **Acetylene: 7 ppm → above the 1 ppm threshold**
- **Hydrogen: 2,850 ppm** (very high; plus CH4 7,400, C2H4 16,650, C2H6 5,470 ppm — TDCG far into IEEE C57.104 Condition 4)

The C2H2 > 1 ppm trigger fires, and WO 1000051 is OLTC/inspection work, so it **moves to the earliest possible date regardless of calendar load**. (The automated DGA fault-classification tool was unavailable, but the gas pattern — ethylene-dominant with elevated methane/ethane, trace acetylene — is characteristic of high-temperature thermal faulting, consistent with the WO's suspected OLTC contact coking.)

## Recommendation

**WO 1000051 — do it alone, as soon as possible; do not defer to a next planned outage.**

Why:
1. The acetylene trigger (7 ppm > 1 ppm) explicitly overrides calendar-based scheduling for OLTC/inspection work.
2. Hydrogen and the hydrocarbon gases are at Condition-4 levels, indicating an active, severe thermal fault — waiting for a future outage bundle carries real risk of in-service failure.
3. There is nothing to bundle it with, so there's no outage-count saving to be gained by waiting.
4. The only "live" candidate task (oil sampling) is already part of this visit, so the single outage clears everything currently on the asset.

Suggested next steps: approve 1000051, set a scheduled start at the earliest crew availability, add a labor plan so hours are tracked, and pull a fresh oil sample beforehand since the last DGA data is from January 2024.
